title: Ultimate RAG Bootcamp: Building Traditional to Agentic Systems with Cloud Deployment
_comment_overview: PARAPHRASED from the krishnaik.in landing page and its accompanying checkout description — never copy sponsor marketing prose verbatim. Facts (fee, module count, framework list, five capstones, deployment targets) are used as-is; the 'move beyond theory' / 'ultimate' sales language is not reproduced.
overview: A 4-5 month live weekend cohort that takes practitioners with existing Python, NLP and deep learning grounding from RAG foundations through to production-grade agentic retrieval systems. Seventeen modules move through document parsing, the LangChain/LlamaIndex/Haystack framework landscape, hybrid search and reranking, multimodal and structured RAG, conversational memory, agentic RAG with ReAct-style agents, and the Model Context Protocol, closing with Docker, Kubernetes and AWS EKS deployment. Learners build five progressively harder projects, from a basic RAG Q&A API to a multimodal assistant and an MCP-powered code review agent.
_comment_category: Primary is RAG/retrieval engineering — 12 of 17 modules are framework, parsing, retrieval-technique or multimodal RAG content. 'Agentic AI' secondary for the dedicated agentic RAG modules (12-13) and MCP module (16); 'MLOps / LLMOps' secondary for the production RAG module (14, Docker/FastAPI/CI-CD/monitoring); 'Cloud' secondary for the AWS EKS deployment target. Same convention as production-ai-llm-engineering, which also carries RAG+agents but is primaried on the LLM-engineering spine rather than the agentic minority.
_comment_level: The page states explicit prerequisites — good Python coding knowledge, basics of NLP and deep learning, basic knowledge of generative AI — which rules out a pure-beginner anchor, same reasoning as the sibling agentic-ai-agentops-bootcamp-3-0. The curriculum genuinely spans from RAG foundations (module 1) to agentic/production systems (modules 12-17), hence level_range; `level` alone is what fusion_rank scores.
_comment_price: ₹6999.00 stated inclusive of GST on the checkout page. Own-site cohort pricing, not coupon-driven, so a number is safe here. Band 'mid' per §2 (₹3,000-9,999) — notably the cheapest of the Krish Naik Academy live bootcamps curated so far.
_comment_rating: No star rating or review count published on either the landing page or the checkout page. Null, not guessed — the validator's null-rating warning is expected.

format._comment_duration: The Course Overview meta line states 'Duration : 4-5 months'; the top hero badge separately says '5 Months'; the sales-prose overview opens with 'a 4-month, project-driven program' and later says 'This 5 months, this intensive program...'. Build retrieval systems with LangChain, LlamaIndex and Haystack, covering ingestion, embeddings, advanced retrievers, hybrid search and framework integration
Parse and pre-process multi-format documents using tools like LlamaParse and Unstructured.io, and apply semantic chunking techniques
Orchestrate graph-based LLM workflows and stateful chatbots with LangGraph, including production-ready human-in-the-loop feedback
Apply enhanced retrieval techniques — hybrid dense and sparse search, reranking, query expansion and HyDE — to improve retrieval performance
Extend RAG across modalities and structured data sources, integrating SQL databases, APIs and JSON/CSV alongside text, images, tables, audio and video
Implement long-term conversational memory, personalization, context optimization and adaptive dialogue flows for contextual RAG
Develop agentic RAG systems using ReAct, tool calling and chain-of-thought reasoning, including multi-agent collaboration, Self-RAG and Graph RAG
Build custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and integrate MCP with Claude and Cursor IDE using LangChain and Docker
Deploy scalable RAG pipelines to production with Docker, FastAPI, Kubernetes and AWS EKS, including CI/CD, monitoring and observability

_comment_projects: Five named projects, stated consistently in both the 'Projects You'll Build' section and the standalone Hands-on list. No version skew here, unlike the sibling agentops course's module-count discrepancy.
_comment_skills: 35 entries exceeds the schema's 30-item guidance, matching the sponsor's own dense 'What You Will Learn' + module list breadth. Bundled published phrases (e.g. 'LangChain, LlamaIndex & Haystack', 'Docker, FastAPI, Kubernetes, and AWS EKS') were split into discrete named tools per §1; every entry maps to a real module.
_comment_career_roles: INFERRED from the stated audience ('AI engineers, ML practitioners, and developers who want to move beyond theory and master production-grade RAG systems') and the MCP-integrated code-review capstone. Card field only, never embedded.
_comment_ladder: Curator-built edge, not a vendor claim — the page names no specific prior course, only skill prerequisites (Python, NLP/deep-learning fundamentals, GenAI basics). Same justification as production-ai-llm-engineering's prereq edge: ultimate-data-science-ai-engineering-3-0 delivers exactly those fundamentals over 12 months. related_ids point to the catalog's other GenAI/RAG/agentic programs for comparison shopping.
